findings.minimal_fix: Nest member accesses under props.externalMemoryProperties (e.g., props.externalMemoryProperties.externalMemoryFeatures, props.externalMemoryProperties.exportFromImportedHandleTypes, and props.externalMemoryProperties.compatibleHandleTypes).
findings.reason: VkExternalBufferProperties in Vulkan 1.1 core (vulkan_core.h) embeds VkExternalMemoryProperties externalMemoryProperties. Accessing externalMemoryFeatures, exportFromImportedHandleTypes, and compatibleHandleTypes directly as members of VkExternalBufferProperties fails compilation. Counterexample: Compiling with standard Vulkan 1.1 headers produces compiler error 'struct VkExternalBufferProperties has no member named externalMemoryFeatures'.

findings.minimal_fix: Set info.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT | VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT; (or the specific buffer usage under evaluation) before querying properties.
findings.reason: info.usage is left 0. Vulkan specification requires usage to be a valid non-zero combination of VkBufferUsageFlagBits (VUID-VkPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferInfo-usage-requiredbitmask). Leaving usage as zero violates valid usage and causes drivers to return zero capability flags or validation failures. Counterexample: Calling vkGetPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferProperties with usage=0 triggers Vulkan validation error and returns exportable=false on compliant drivers.

findings.minimal_fix: Check res < VK_SUCCESS instead of res != VK_SUCCESS to allow VK_INCOMPLETE as valid non-fatal completion.
findings.reason: Vulkan enumeration APIs (vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices, vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties) return VK_INCOMPLETE (positive success code) when buffer sizing or counts change. Testing res != VK_SUCCESS treats VK_INCOMPLETE as a fatal failure, incorrectly zeroing gpu_count or clearing all discovered extensions. Counterexample: If a driver returns VK_INCOMPLETE on extension enumeration, exts.clear() wipes extension properties and falsely drops VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf.

findings.minimal_fix: Add runtime check if (prop.apiVersion >= VK_API_VERSION_1_1) before invoking Vulkan 1.1 calls, or dynamically resolve entrypoints using vkGetInstanceProcAddr.
findings.reason: Compile-time header guard #if defined(VK_VERSION_1_1) verifies header availability but does not verify runtime driver support (prop.apiVersion >= VK_API_VERSION_1_1) or resolve entrypoints via vkGetInstanceProcAddr. Calling Vulkan 1.1 entrypoints on a Vulkan 1.0 runtime results in null dereferences or dynamic symbol resolution failures. Counterexample: Executing against a Vulkan 1.0 loader or driver crashes when calling statically resolved vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2.

findings.minimal_fix: Validate dedicated_vram_p2p across multi-device topology receipts and peer capabilities rather than looping over memory types of a single device in isolation.
findings.reason: The test evaluates dedicated_vram_p2p against individual memory types on an isolated single device. This equates single-device local VRAM residency with multi-device P2P transfer, while falsely rejecting valid discrete GPUs because any additional host-visible memory type (e.g., ReBAR) triggers an error. Counterexample: A discrete GPU claiming P2P with two memory types (Type 0: non-host-visible VRAM, Type 1: ReBAR host-visible VRAM) triggers a false positive rejection on Type 1.

findings.minimal_fix: Add explicit assertions checking that external_buffer_capabilities, external_semaphore_capabilities, and external_fence_capabilities contain valid DMA_BUF_EXT and SYNC_FD entries.
findings.reason: The test validator fails to check external_buffer_capabilities, external_semaphore_capabilities, or external_fence_capabilities. It never validates DMA_BUF or sync primitive availability, exportability, or compatibility flags. Counterexample: An artifact providing empty external_buffer_capabilities: [] passes validator checks with mock_contract_validator_pass: True and return code 0.

safety_checks: Source contains fatal compilation defect props.externalMemoryFeatures and must not be compiled or executed until nested under externalMemoryProperties.
Zero-usage buffer capability query violates Vulkan valid usage (VUID-VkPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferInfo-usage-requiredbitmask) and cannot represent valid driver capabilities.
Host-visible or imported buffer sharing must never be claimed or aliased as dedicated physical VRAM peer-to-peer (P2P) transfer.
Advertised device extensions do not prove cross-vendor legal allocation import, synchronization contracts, or physical PCIe bus routing.
Untrusted driver facts and cross-vendor DMA-BUF transfers remain NOT_CHECKED without verified physical hardware receipts and directed peer access queries.
